table1_E17_5_long_bone_length_mm.note: ALL FOUR TREND SHORTER AND THE TIBIA IS SIGNIFICANT AT P=0.02. The abstract says alterations in length were NOT detected at E17.5; the paper's own Table 1 is softer than that.

table2_BrdU_E17_5_percent_labelled_nucle.note: chondrocyte Tgfbr2 loss TRENDS TOWARD INCREASED proliferation; the ligand null DECREASES it

table3_postnatal_bone_length_cm.caveat: NO standard deviations, NO n and NO P values are given for Table 3; the text says these are 'the few Col2acre+;Tgfbr2loxP/loxP mice that survived birth'. Treat as representative measurements, not a powered comparison.

authors_own_conclusion_on_compartment: 'The data suggest that any role of Tgfbr2 in embryonic long bones is mediated indirectly through cells that do not express Col2a-Cre, likely cells in the perichondrium as previously suggested (Alvarez et al., 2001, 2002).' Eighteen years before sedes2022 reached the same place from fibrillin-1.
answer_to_the_gap: SHORTER. Progressive, absent at postnatal day 3, present from day 7 through 12 weeks, roughly -17 to -33 per cent in PROXIMAL long bones, with METATARSALS and SKULL spared - which the authors use to argue the effect is not systemic or isometric.
